**1.003: Your microphones in your order, and no more lost words.**

- **Microphones** (Settings → Microphones): every mic Hebrish has seen on this computer, with a name you give it and a type (built-in, headset, wireless headset, shotgun, lav, dynamic and more). Put them in order and pick **Preferred order** as the microphone: each take uses the first one that is connected, and the system default when none is. A mic plugged in between takes is picked up. On Ubuntu mics are recognised by their vendor and product id, so a USB mic stays the same mic on any port.
- **The last words after Stop arrive.** The last few seconds of a take, decoded after you stop, were sometimes taken for silence when spoken softly and dropped without a word. They are now judged against the rest of the take.
- **Quiet takes are no longer "No speech".** On a mic at a low level (a headset at its default gain), whole takes could be rejected as silent. A take now counts as speech when it rises clearly above its own background noise.
- **The tray shows when more is coming:** after you stop, the icon turns amber with three dots until the last words are in.
- **Slightly longer pieces** when inserting as you go: Fast ~4 s, Normal ~6 s, Relaxed ~10 s (were 3, 5 and 8). If you were on a preset, you move to its new value.
- Ubuntu 26.04 .deb and a portable Windows zip. Not yet tested on Windows hardware. Downloads: [hebrish.app/download](https://hebrish.app/download).
